own_solution.law: The intercepted power is IA cos(theta). Absorption transfers normal momentum E cos(theta)/c per photon, and specular reflection transfers twice this amount. Therefore F = (1 + Rf)IA cos²(theta)/c and v = Ft/m. Using c = 2.998 × 10^8 m/s and t = 86400 s gives F = 6.65444 × 10^-4 N and v = 114.988659 m/s.
assumptions: The stated illumination and reflection fraction remain constant during the exposure.
The stated nonrelativistic regime permits treating the intensity and incidence angle as constant.
The mirror starts at rest, and only the normal radiation force accelerates it along the rail.
Heating and its possible recoil effects are neglected as stipulated.

notes: I revise the pass-1 rendering objection: the authors explicitly identify T8261 and TB1C7 as numeral-free controls, whose intended transformation removes the number and unit; they do not claim these are numbered minimal pairs. Both actual minimal_pair_with claims preserve 470 W/m² and change the attachment as intended. The photon-energy cancellation is correct when energy is expressed consistently in joules: photon arrival rate varies inversely with energy and momentum per photon varies proportionally. All three listed photon energies therefore give 114.989 m/s. Both relevant intensity additions give 136.344, 153.592 and 187.267 m/s for 260, 470 and 880 W/m² respectively. Earlier illumination has no retained effect under the stated initial-rest and neglected-heating conditions. Screen illumination is disconnected from the mirror. The governing relations have the correct dimensions after converting hours and kilometres to SI units, and every certified answer has adequate precision.
